title: Voz pasiva: extracción de plata y oro

sections.content: Passive voice keeps the mineral, the process, or the money as the subject — exactly what mining history needs, since the same silver moves through many hands. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En 1545 fue descubierto el yacimiento de plata del Cerro Rico de Potosí.
items.english: In 1545, the Cerro Rico de Potosí silver deposit was discovered.

items.spanish: Enormes cantidades de plata fueron extraídas de esa montaña y enviadas a España.
items.english: Enormous quantities of silver were extracted from that mountain and sent to Spain.

items.spanish: A partir de 1554, la producción de plata fue transformada por un nuevo método inventado por Bartolomé de Medina.
items.english: Starting in 1554, silver production was transformed by a new method invented by Bartolomé de Medina.

items.spanish: Gran parte de esa plata fue acuñada en monedas, los llamados 'reales de a ocho'.
items.english: Much of that silver was minted into coins, the so-called 'pieces of eight'.

sections.content: Notice how each sentence keeps a physical thing (el yacimiento, la plata, la producción, esa plata) as the grammatical subject, letting a single paragraph trace silver's whole journey — discovered, extracted, processed, minted — without ever needing 'los españoles' as the subject.
